title: frozen backbone with two-sided Mirror task views
hypothesis: Given a frozen shared linear backbone, a two-coordinate input/output Mirror address will recover a new task in the matched two-sided Givens family at comparable quality to rank-2 LoRA using no more than one quarter of its incremental inference bytes; an independent task map will expose the need for private parameters.
physical_object: One shared 16x8 linear map and output bias, treated as a pretrained Task-0 backbone and charged in all inference payloads
mirror_coordinate: Two learned float32 Givens angles: one rotates the first input-coordinate pair before the shared map, and one rotates the first output-coordinate pair after it
logical_multiplicity: Task-0 function plus one new task-conditioned function, with the shared physical map frozen
targeted_literature: Infinite-Parameter LLMs: Generating and Adapting Weights from Live Data (arXiv:2609.18842)
Ouroboros: Dynamic Weight Generation for Recursive Transformers via Input-Conditioned LoRA Modulation (arXiv:2604.02051)
controls: one-sided input-only Mirror coordinate as MA-186 mechanism control
shared hypernetwork generating rank-2 LoRA with non-degenerate factor initialization
independent full Task-1 weights as upper control
task: Synthetic 16D-to-8D linear task. The shared backbone is the exact Task-0 teacher map and bias, isolating new-task adaptation from base-pretraining error. In the aligned condition, Task-1 is generated by one input-pair Givens rotation and one output-pair Givens rotation of that same map. In the unrelated condition, Task-1 has an independent random matrix and bias. Task-0 retention is measured before and after adaptation.

adaptation.batching: full-batch over a nested fixed training set for each budget
adaptation.selection_metric: mean held-out Task-1 MSE across methods and both task families at 64 examples; tie-break by registered bytes and Task-0 retention

storage.authority: actual serialized inference payload bytes and actual serialized resumable checkpoint bytes
storage.inference_serialization: deterministic packed binary tensor records, including method, dimensions, task ID, every name/dtype/shape field, metadata and raw tensor bytes
storage.resume_serialization: torch.save envelope with complete inference state and optimizer state
report: incremental inference bytes per new task
paid_objects: both Mirror angles and task ID
names, dtypes, dimensions, shapes and method metadata
optimizer moments and step state in resume bytes

success_gate: At 64 examples on all three fresh aligned worlds, two-sided Mirror held-out Task-1 MSE <=1.10x rank-2 LoRA, incremental inference bytes <=0.25x rank-2 LoRA, and absolute Task-0 MSE increase <=0.01. Report all 16/64/256-example points. If rank-1 or the shared hypernetwork matches at comparable bytes/compute, do not claim a Mirror-specific advantage.
failure_gate: Both development worlds miss either the <=1.10x rank-2 LoRA quality ratio or <=0.25x byte ratio at 256 examples; keep fresh worlds sealed.
boundaries: One new skill after a frozen exact synthetic base; not a sequential retention benchmark
Fixed 200-update schedule at each nested data budget
Synthetic linear maps only; no language-model or natural continual-learning claim
Fixed-budget/sample-efficiency evidence is not a capacity claim
